what_matters.head: Nvidia reports Q3 results after tonight's New York close, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress.
what_matters.detail: Results come at about 1:20 p.m. Pacific on 17 Nov (about 05:20 SGT Wednesday), with the call at 06:00 SGT (company 8-K). The company forecast revenue of $108.0B, plus or minus 2%, and a gross margin of 74.0%, plus or minus half a point. 42 analysts expect about $108.7B. Options trading implies a move of about Â±9% either way by Friday, from Friday's close (Investopedia).

what_matters.head: The chip fund fell 5.4% on Monday, about 1.6 times its usual daily move. TSMC fell 6.3% (2.4 times usual), ASML 5.9% and Navitas 12.0%.
what_matters.detail: Reuters said fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation soured enthusiasm for AI stocks before Nvidia's results. During the session, a person familiar told CNBC that Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back (one report). Investing.com said traders were also unwinding bets on Nvidia's rivals, such as Micron and AMD.

what_matters.tag_note: US chip rule Â· Singapore named
what_matters.head: The US now requires a licence for advanced AI chips shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, under a Commerce Department rule issued on Monday.
what_matters.detail: The rule targets Chinese companies renting computing power in data centres outside China. Overseas data centres serving China-headquartered companies need a licence, and existing operators have 90 days after the rule takes effect to get one (Investing.com). Each licence is reviewed case by case (AP). Coverage of Monday's session said the rule added to the pressure on chip stocks (Motley Fool). This morning Singapore's Frencken fell 3.9% and AEM 2.9%, and Malaysia's YTL Power nearly 10% (Reuters).

recent.headline: Nvidia reports Q3 results after tonight's New York close, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress.
Nvidia reports Q3 results after Tuesday's New York close, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress.
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive and left its board, effective immediately. Nvidia closed down 4.3%, about 1.8 times its usual daily move.
Nvidia fell about 8% after hours on Wednesday, after the Wall Street Journal reported that its board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia fell another 5.5% on Tuesday, about 2.3 times its usual daily move, on twice its average volume. It is down 18.3% over five sessions.
